props.title: 20 Feet from Stardom

sections.content: **20 Feet from Stardom (2013)** (2013) revolutionized how we see backup singers, finally giving these vocal powerhouses their moment in the spotlight. Director Morgan Neville expertly weaves together the stories of Darlene Love, Merry Clayton, and Lisa Fischer - artists who shaped pop music history from the shadows. The film's raw emotional power hits hardest during Clayton's isolated vocal track from **Gimme Shelter** - her haunting wails on "rape, murder" will send chills down your spine. Like Standing in the Shadows of Motown (2002), it reveals the hidden figures behind countless hits.

sections.content: The film brilliantly captures the bittersweet reality of almost-fame. Judith Hill's story particularly resonates - after backing Michael Jackson and being slated for his "This Is It" tour, she seemed destined for solo stardom. Her journey mirrors countless talents who've lived just outside the spotlight, like the session musicians in The Wrecking Crew (2008) who secretly played for everyone from The Beach Boys to The Monkees.

Beyond music, **20 Feet from Stardom** exposes the racial and gender dynamics of the music industry. Many backup singers, particularly Black women, watched white artists rocket to fame performing their arrangements and styles. This echoes themes from **Cadillac Records** (2008), showing how the music industry historically exploited Black talent while promoting white faces. SUBHEAD: The Evolution of Music Documentaries

sections.content: This Oscar-winning documentary helped usher in a new era of music films that celebrate unsung heroes. Its influence can be seen in **Summer of Soul** (2021), which resurfaces forgotten footage of the 1969 Harlem Cultural Festival, and **The Beatles: Get Back** (2021), which gives unprecedented attention to the band's support staff and technical crew.
